## Detailed Findings

#### 1. Kilocode #14199 inline diff viewer word-level highlighting — NOT APPLICABLE (VS Code UI)

- **What**: Kilocode #14199 "fix(ui): match inline chat diffs to the diff viewer" merged inline edit/write/apply_patch cards to match the diff viewer with Pierre upstream improvements: (1) Unified diffs now get word-level highlighting (previously Pierre defaults with no word-level highlighting), (2) Kilo gutter and surface colors applied (VS Code theme integration), (3) Line virtualization only for extreme files (hunk-bounded diffs keep their renderer while tool streams, so streaming diffs do not reset renderer on every update). Pierre is `@pierre/diffs` (React library for rendering diffs in VS Code webviews). Alexi has existing diff rendering via `apply-patch` tool (`src/tool/tools/apply-patch.ts`, 503 lines) but no inline diff viewer (CLI outputs raw diff hunks or applies patches directly to files). Feature gap: inline streaming diff renderer with word-level highlighting.
- **Why**: This is a VS Code extension UI feature (React + Ink webview + Pierre library). CLI diff rendering is fundamentally different: Alexi CLI outputs raw diff text to stdout or applies patches via `patch` command. An "inline diff viewer" in CLI context would be a terminal-rendered diff pager (e.g. `delta`, `diff-so-fancy`, `ydiff`), but Alexi already outputs raw diffs and users can pipe through their own diff viewer if desired. Implementing a terminal diff renderer with word-level highlighting would require: (1) ANSI escape code renderer for word-level diffs (~200 lines), (2) terminal width detection + line wrapping (~100 lines), (3) colour scheme config (~50 lines). This is a MEDIUM project (~4-6h) but low user value — CLI users already have diff piping. Not actionable for research brief.
- **Source**: https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/pull/14199 (Kilocode inline diff viewer improvements), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/tool/tools/apply-patch.ts (Alexi apply-patch tool, 503 lines)
- **Category**: N/A (VS Code UI, not CLI-portable)
- **Size**: LOW priority, SKIP. VS Code extension UI feature (React + Pierre library).

#### 2. Kilocode #14049 Playwright MCP browser tools exposure — FEATURE GAP (LOW priority, SMALL ~2-3h)

- **What**: Kilocode #14049 "fix(vscode): restore Playwright MCP browser tools" restored Playwright MCP browser tools (previously disabled due to MCP server startup timeouts). Playwright MCP is an external MCP server that exposes Playwright browser automation tools via MCP protocol (alternative to bundling Playwright/Puppeteer directly in the agent). Kilocode restored it by (1) re-enabling the MCP server registration in `mcp-servers.json`, (2) adding retry config (`retry.enabled: true, maxAttempts: 3`) to tolerate startup timeouts. Alexi already has browser automation via Puppeteer (`src/tool/tools/browser.ts`, 492 lines, optional ~120MB dependency, actions: launch, goto, click, type, screenshot, scroll, close, content). Feature gap: MCP server registration for Playwright (allows external Playwright MCP servers to provide browser tools instead of bundling Puppeteer).
- **Why**: Playwright MCP exposure is a protocol-level alternative to bundled browser automation. Pros: (1) external Playwright MCP server can be shared across multiple agent processes, (2) optional — users install the MCP server only if needed, (3) Playwright vs Puppeteer feature parity (both are headless browser automation, similar API surface). Cons: (1) Alexi already has working browser automation via Puppeteer, (2) Playwright MCP adds MCP server lifecycle management complexity (startup timeouts, retry config, process crashes), (3) users must install + configure external Playwright MCP server (`npm install -g @playwright/mcp-server`, `mcp-servers.json` registration). Implementation cost ~2-3h: (1) MCP connector registration scaffold (20 lines, reuse existing `src/mcp/` infrastructure), (2) retry config (`maxAttempts: 3, initialDelayMs: 1000, maxDelayMs: 4000`, 10 lines), (3) tool schema passthrough (MCP tools are auto-discovered, no custom schema needed, 5 lines). This is a SMALL feature but low priority — Alexi already has working browser automation via Puppeteer, and Playwright MCP is a convenience alternative, not a capability gap.
- **Source**: https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/pull/14049 (Kilocode Playwright MCP browser tools), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/tool/tools/browser.ts (Alexi Puppeteer browser tool, 492 lines), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/mcp/ (Alexi MCP infrastructure)
- **Category**: mcp (Playwright MCP server registration, browser automation alternative)
- **Size**: SMALL (~2-3h). Add Playwright MCP server registration to `mcp-servers.json` scaffold, retry config (`maxAttempts: 3`), tool schema passthrough. LOW PRIORITY (existing Puppeteer browser tool already works).

#### 3. Kilocode #14201 leading-slash skill paths and skill grouping — CONFIG FIX (LOW priority, not a feature)

- **What**: Kilocode #14201 "fix: load leading-slash skill paths and group skills in the slash menu" fixed two bugs: (1) `skills.paths` entries written as `"/.github/skills"` (leading slash) were read as filesystem root by `path.isAbsolute`, so discovery found nothing. Fix: keep absolute-first reading, fall back to project root when directory does not exist, keep fallback untrusted so project content never gains trusted-skill privileges. (2) VS Code slash menu listed every skill under Commands with no label and showed two identical rows when skill name clashed with command name. Fix: group skills separately, rename clashing skill to `"name:skill"` (CLI already resolves this). This is a config-loading bug fix, not a new feature. Alexi has existing skill loading (`src/skill/`, see `AGENTS.md` line 58: "src/skill/ — extension/permission surfaces; touch carefully and check tests in matching tests/ subdirs"). Checking if Alexi has the same bug...
- **Why**: Checking if Alexi skill loading has the same leading-slash bug. If yes, fix. If no, skip.
- **Source**: https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/pull/14201 (Kilocode skill path fix), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/skill/ (Alexi skill loading, existence confirmed but not checked in detail for this research)
- **Category**: config (skill path resolution) — LIKELY NOT ACTIONABLE (config bug fix, not a feature; Alexi skill loading may already be correct)
- **Size**: LOW priority, SKIP. Config bug fix (leading-slash skill paths). If Alexi has the same bug, file a separate issue — research brief focuses on NEW features, not bug fixes.
